chapters.name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
learn: Sessions and presidents: Calcutta 1906 (Naoroji, Swaraj), Lahore 1929 (Nehru, Purna Swaraj), Karachi 1931 (Fundamental Rights), Gaya 1922 (C. R. Das), Bankipur 1912
Firsts: Badruddin Tyabji (first Muslim president), Annie Besant (first woman president, 1917)
Safety-valve theory and Lala Lajpat Rai; Aurobindo's New Lamps for Old
Pre-Congress bodies and founders: Indian Association (Surendranath Banerjee, 1876), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Madras Mahajan Sabha; Servants of India Society (Gokhale, 1905)
Order of events: Surat Split 1907, Minto-Morley 1909, Home Rule 1916, Kheda 1918
chapters.note: One of the most frequent chapters: sessions with president, year and resolution.

chapters.name: Cabinet Mission, Interim Government and Partition
learn: Cabinet Mission members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A. V. Alexander
Interim Government portfolios: Rajendra Prasad - Food and Agriculture, Liaquat Ali Khan - Finance, Jagjivan Ram - Labour
Direct Action Day (16 August 1946); Attlee's statement (20 February 1947); Radcliffe; Indian Independence Act 1947
Order of events 1942-46: Cripps Mission, Quit India, Wavell, Cabinet Mission
chapters.note: Cabinet Mission members and Interim Government portfolios repeat almost verbatim.

chapters.name: Revolutionary Movement
learn: Ghadar Party (USA, 1913), Har Dayal; centres abroad: Yugantar Ashram (San Francisco), Swadesh Sevak Home (Vancouver)
Bhagat Singh: Assembly bomb (1929) with B. K. Dutt; hanged 23 March 1931
Other acts: Chittagong Armoury Raid (Surya Sen), Udham Singh (1940), bomb on Hardinge (1912), Madam Cama at Stuttgart (1907)
Bihar links: Khudiram Bose at Muzaffarpur (1908); Bismil Azimabadi wrote Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna
chapters.note: Asked in most papers.

chapters.name: Champaran Satyagraha
learn: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, 1917, against the tinkathia system (3/20 of land under indigo)
Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi to Champaran
Associates: Rajendra Prasad, J. B. Kripalani; Batak Mian saved Gandhi from poisoning
Champaran Agrarian Committee (1917) with Gandhi as a member
chapters.note: Bihar-specific and asked in almost every paper, sometimes twice in one paper.

chapters.name: Freedom Fighters, Books and Journals
learn: Titles: Deshbandhu (C. R. Das), Frontier Gandhi (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan)
Journals and editors: Al-Hilal (Azad), Comrade (Mohammad Ali), Indian Opinion (Gandhi), Bengalee (Surendranath Banerjee), Bahishkrit Bharat (Ambedkar)
Books: Unhappy India (Lala Lajpat Rai)
Parties and founders: Forward Bloc, Independent Labour Party (Ambedkar), Khaksars, Indian National Liberal Federation
chapters.note: Usually match-the-following.

chapters.name: Subhas Bose and the INA
learn: Forward Bloc (1939); first called Netaji in Germany; "Chalo Delhi"
Provisional Government of Free India (1943); Andaman and Nicobar renamed Shaheed and Swaraj
INA officers (Shahnawaz Khan, Mohan Singh, Prem Sehgal) and the INA trials (Bhulabhai Desai)

chapters.name: Individual Satyagraha and Quit India Movement
learn: Individual Satyagraha (1940): Vinoba Bhave first (from Pavnar), Nehru second
Quit India: "Do or Die"; Usha Mehta's Congress Radio
Parallel governments: Satara, Tamluk, Talcher, Ballia
Bihar: Jayaprakash Narayan's escape from Hazaribagh Jail (9 November 1942) and the Azad Dasta
chapters.note: Repeats often, usually with a Bihar angle.

chapters.name: Civil Disobedience and Round Table Conferences
learn: Dandi March: 12 March to 5 April 1930, 24 days; Purna Swaraj Day on 26 January 1930
Gandhi-Irwin Pact: March 1931
Simon Commission boycotted for having no Indian member
Ambedkar attended all three Round Table Conferences
In Bihar the salt satyagraha included refusal of the chowkidari tax

chapters.name: Peasant, Labour and States' People's Movements
learn: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928): Vallabhbhai Patel
Awadh peasant movement: Baba Ramchandra; Swami Vidyanand in Bihar
Praja Mandal movement in the princely states
AITUC founded in 1920

chapters.name: Gandhi and Early Satyagrahas
learn: Ahmedabad mill strike (1918): Gandhi's first hunger strike
Life facts: studied at Samaldas College; first major public speech at BHU (1916)
All India Harijan Sangh (1932)

chapters.name: Non-Cooperation Movement and Swaraj Party
learn: Chauri Chaura (1922), Gorakhpur district
Who joined in the towns; the Justice Party contested council elections
Swaraj Party (1923): C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru; Shri Krishna Singh set up the Swaraj Dal in Bihar

chapters.name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement
learn: Swadeshi and Boycott arose against the Partition of Bengal (1905)
Surendranath Banerjee's remark that the announcement "fell like a bombshell"

chapters.name: Revolt of 1857
learn: Centres and leaders: Jagdishpur in Bihar (Kunwar Singh), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal), Kanpur (Nana Saheb), Bareilly (Khan Bahadur), Faizabad (Maulavi Ahmadullah), Jhansi (Rani Laxmibai)
V. D. Savarkar called it the First War of Indian Independence; other historians: S. N. Sen, Eric Stokes, S. B. Chaudhuri
Causes of failure
chapters.note: Asked in most papers; Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur is the Bihar angle.

chapters.name: Socio-Religious Reform Movements
learn: Founders: Atmiya Sabha and Brahmo Samaj (Ram Mohan Roy), Tattwabodhini Sabha (Debendranath Tagore), Ramakrishna Mission (Vivekananda, 1897)
Vivekananda at Chicago (1893); Jyotiba Phule's Gulamgiri (1873)
Faraizi Movement (Haji Shariatullah); Aligarh movement and Theodore Beck
chapters.note: Usually match organisation with founder.

chapters.name: British Conquest and Expansion
learn: Battles and treaties: Wandiwash (1760), Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Treaty of Salbai (1782)
Clive's dual government in Bengal (1765)
Doctrine of Lapse states: Satara, Sambalpur, Nagpur, Jhansi
Annexation of Sind by Charles Napier (1843)

chapters.name: Governors-General and Administrative Reforms
learn: Lord Mayo: financial decentralisation (1870); first census in 1872
Lytton: Vernacular Press Act, Arms Act, Delhi Durbar of 1877; Ripon: Ilbert Bill
Bentinck: abolition of Sati, suppression of Thugs
Capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi (announced 1911)
chapters.note: Match the Viceroy with the event; Mayo's 1870 resolution was asked twice.

chapters.name: Tribal and Peasant Revolts
learn: Santhal Hul (1855-56): Sidhu and Kanhu
Kol uprising (1831), Chuar revolt, Birsa Munda's Ulgulan (1899-1900)
Indigo revolt and Neel Darpan (Dinabandhu Mitra); Sannyasi Rebellion and Anandamath
chapters.note: Santhal revolt and its leaders repeat; these are the old Bihar-Jharkhand region revolts.

chapters.name: Land Revenue and Economic Impact
learn: Permanent Settlement (Cornwallis, 1793), Ryotwari (Madras), Mahalwari (Holt Mackenzie, 1822)
Dadabhai Naoroji and Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
Opium and the triangular trade between India, China and England

chapters.name: Education and Press under British Rule
learn: Macaulay's Minute (1835), Wood's Despatch (1854), Fort William College (1800)
Vernacular Press Act 1878 (the Gagging Act): by Lytton, repealed by Ripon
Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780)
chapters.note: The Vernacular Press Act repeats.

chapters.name: Constitutional Acts under British Rule
learn: Indian Councils Act 1909: separate electorates
Government of India Act 1935: provincial autonomy, proposed federation; Nehru's "all brakes and no engine" remark

chapters.name: Formation of Bihar Province
learn: Bihar separated from Bengal: 1912; Orissa separated from Bihar: 1936; Jharkhand carved out: 2000
Governors: S. P. Sinha, first Indian Governor of Bihar and Orissa; James David Sifton, first Governor of Bihar (1936)
chapters.note: Bihar-specific: 1912 is one of the most repeated facts in BPSC.

chapters.name: Bihar in the Freedom Struggle
learn: Shri Krishna Singh (Bihar Kesari): Premier from 1937, first Chief Minister; his ministry's resignation in 1938 over political prisoners
Jayaprakash Narayan: Lok Nayak, Azad Dasta, Bihar Socialist Party (1931)
Congress sessions in Bihar: Bankipur 1912 (R. N. Mudholkar), Gaya 1922 (C. R. Das)
Revolutionaries: Sachindra Nath Sanyal and the Patna branch of Anushilan Samiti (1913)
Home Rule in Bihar and Annie Besant's visit; 1942 martyrs
Books and banned writings: Rajendra Prasad's Mahatma Gandhi and Bihar; Gharib Hindustan
chapters.note: Bihar-specific and asked in every paper: learn Bihar leaders with their titles and movements.

chapters.name: Medieval Bihar and Its Monuments
learn: Bakhtiyar Khalji and the start of Turk rule in Bihar
Karnat dynasty of Mithila and the growth of Maithili
Firdausia Sufi order and Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri
Dutch factory at Patna (1632)
Monuments: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram, Padri Ki Haveli in Patna
chapters.note: Bihar-specific.

chapters.name: Press and Education in Bihar
learn: First newspapers: Patna Harkara (first from Bihar), Sarva Hitaishi (first Hindi daily)
Institutions and founding years: Patna College (1863), Patna Women's College (1940), revived Nalanda University (2014)
chapters.note: Bihar-specific.

chapters.name: Kisan Sabha and Peasant Movements in Bihar
learn: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati: leader of the Kisan Sabha movement in Bihar
Bakasht movement (1937-38)
His newspaper Lok Sangraha
chapters.note: Bihar-specific: Sahajanand Saraswati is asked in paper after paper.

chapters.name: Nalanda and Vikramshila Universities
learn: Vikramshila (Bhagalpur): founded by Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty; a Vajrayana centre
Nalanda acharyas: Nagarjuna, Shilabhadra, Shantarakshita
Other centres: Valabhi, Taxila (Kautilya)
chapters.note: Bihar-specific.

chapters.name: Buddhism and Jainism
learn: Buddhist councils: place, patron and president (Rajgir - Mahakashyapa, Vaishali, Pataliputra, Kashmir - Kanishka)
Places in the Buddha's life: enlightenment at Bodh Gaya
Jain Triratna: right faith, right knowledge, right conduct
Ajivikas: Makkhali Gosala and the doctrine of niyati
chapters.note: Buddhist councils are asked very often, and three of the four venues are in Bihar.

chapters.name: Mahajanapadas and Rise of Magadha
learn: Capitals: Rajagriha (Girivraja) first, then Pataliputra
Dynasty order: Haryanka (Bimbisara), Shishunaga, Nanda
Bimbisara's physician Jivaka
Magadha was the region south of the Ganga
chapters.note: Bihar-specific: Magadha is Bihar's own ancient history and is asked in most papers.

chapters.name: Prehistory and Indus Valley Civilisation
learn: Sites and finds: Lothal (port city, Gujarat), Kalibangan (ploughed field)
What the Harappans did not know: the horse
Beginning of iron use in the subcontinent
chapters.note: Lothal is the most repeated site.

chapters.name: Post-Mauryan and Sangam Age
learn: Chronological order: Maurya, Shunga, Kanva, Kushana
Kushana trade with the Roman empire
Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription and the repair of Sudarshan Lake
Sangam kingdoms and capitals: Chera capital Vanji (Karur)

chapters.name: Ancient Literature and Science
learn: Authors and works: Bharavi - Kiratarjuniya, Kamandaka - Nitisara, Vishakhadatta (playwright)
Scientists: Charaka (medicine), Brahmagupta (mathematics), Varahamihira (astronomy/astrology)
Amarakosha terms for types of land

chapters.name: Gupta Empire and Vakatakas
learn: Samudragupta and Meghavarman of Sri Lanka (monastery at Gaya)
Chandragupta II and the Ramagupta story
Travellers: Fa-Hien under Chandragupta II, Hiuen Tsang under Harsha
Vakatakas: Vindhyashakti and Pravarasena I

chapters.name: Harsha and the Vardhana Dynasty
learn: Pushyabhuti founded the Vardhana dynasty
Contemporaries of Harsha: Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa
Ancient place names and their present States: Karnasuvarna, Pragjyotisha, Girnar, Pratishthana

chapters.name: Mauryan Empire
learn: Chandragupta Maurya: founder; linked with Vishnugupta (Kautilya) and Sudarshan Lake
Ashoka: pillar edicts in Brahmi script, Dharma Mahamatras, Sanchi
Match rulers with achievements across dynasties (Rajendra I - Gangaikonda, Harsha - Prayag assembly)

chapters.name: Vedic Period and Indian Philosophy
learn: Women seers of the Rigveda: Ghosha, Apala, Vishvavara (Gargi is later Vedic)
Six schools of philosophy: Vaisheshika propounded the atomic theory

chapters.name: Delhi Sultanate
learn: Balban: blood and iron policy, Nauroz, title Zill-i-Ilahi, Tughril Khan's revolt
Iltutmish: completed the Qutub Minar, investiture from the Caliph
Administration: muqaddam or chaudhari as village headman
Malik Kafur (Hazar Dinari); Bahlol Lodi had the longest reign
chapters.note: Asked in almost every paper; Balban is the favourite.

chapters.name: Mughal Empire
learn: Babur: founder, use of cannon; battles of Panipat and Haldighati with opponents
Books and authors: Ain-i-Akbari (Abul Fazl), Tabaqat-i-Akbari (Nizamuddin Ahmad)
Visitors and ports: Thomas Roe under Jahangir; Surat as Bab-ul-Makka
Humayun and Sher Khan in Bihar; Aurangzeb and the Anglo-Mughal war; Mughal fathers and sons

chapters.name: Chola and Vijayanagara Empires
learn: Cholas: Vijayalaya the founder; village self-government
Vijayanagara: Harihara and Bukka (1336); Krishnadevaraya founded Nagalapuram

chapters.name: Medieval Literature and Sources
learn: Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi (Barani, Shams Siraj Afif)
Futuhat-i-Alamgiri (Ishwardas Nagar); Chach Nama and its Persian translator

chapters.name: Bhakti and Sufi Movements
learn: Works of Tulsidas (Gitavali, Vinay Patrika, Kavitavali) and Surdas (Sahitya Lahari)
Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis in northern India

chapters.name: Marathas
learn: Ashta Pradhan: Peshwa (prime minister), Amatya (finance), Sachiv (correspondence), Sumant (foreign affairs)
chapters.note: Asked in consecutive papers.

chapters.name: Ancient Art and Architecture
learn: Gupta art: Deogarh temple and Garhwa sculptures
Buddhist structures: stupa, chaitya, vihara
Ajanta paintings: Bodhisattva Padmapani
chapters.note: The Deogarh-Garhwa question was repeated word for word.

chapters.name: Art and Culture of Bihar
learn: Madhubani (Mithila) painting; Sujini embroidery
Fairs and festivals with place: Sonepur cattle fair (Ganga-Gandak confluence), Bihula festival (Bhagalpur)
Religious sites: Takht Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib
chapters.note: Bihar-specific.

chapters.name: Medieval Architecture and Monuments
learn: Monuments and builders: Kabuli Bagh mosque (Babur), Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra (Aibak), Allahabad Fort (Akbar), Itmad-ud-Daulah's tomb (Nur Jahan)
Mughal art terms: pietra dura; Akbar's karkhanas for painting
UNESCO World Heritage monuments such as Qutb Minar and Red Fort

chapters.name: World History
learn: Explorers and their countries of birth: Columbus, Magellan, Drake, Cartier
Mesopotamia as the oldest civilisation
Manhattan Project; Egypt-Israel peace treaty (1979)
chapters.note: A minor area: about one question in some papers.

chapters.name: States of Matter and Solutions
learn: Solutions: concentration, boiling-point elevation, Raoult's law for ideal solutions
States: triple point, liquefying gases (low temperature, high pressure)
Avogadro's law; sublimation to separate naphthalene from sand

chapters.name: Chemistry in Everyday Life
learn: Everyday chemicals: quicklime (CaO), limestone in cement, soda-acid fire extinguisher, breathalyser (potassium dichromate)
Colours and materials: strontium for red fireworks, glow-in-the-dark pigments, indium tin oxide
Medicines: cisplatin (cancer), levonorgestrel (contraceptive); explosives such as HMX
chapters.note: Asked in most papers, increasingly on modern materials.

chapters.name: Carbon and Organic Chemistry
learn: Diamond and graphite: allotropes, differences, lab-grown diamonds from graphite
Common organic compounds: acetic acid (vinegar), oxalic acid, urea, fructose (sweetest sugar)
Fermentation: zymase converts glucose to ethanol
CO₂ turns limewater milky; electrophiles accept electron pairs
chapters.note: Lab-grown diamonds were asked in consecutive papers.

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
learn: pH scale: pH = -log[H⁺]; base above 7; each unit is a tenfold change
Litmus tests; acids on metal carbonates release CO₂; why dry HCl does not affect litmus
Amphoteric oxides: Al₂O₃, ZnO
Acetic acid in vinegar

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Electrochemistry
learn: Physical versus chemical changes; exothermic versus endothermic processes
Catalysts, promoters and inhibitors; nickel in hydrogenation of oils
Electrochemistry: Faraday constant, conductivity on dilution, electrode potential and reducing power

chapters.name: Fuels and Hydrogen Energy
learn: Composition: methane in biogas, butane in LPG; carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion
Tetraethyllead as the old anti-knock additive
Hydrogen: grey/green colour codes, storage as compressed gas or hydrides

chapters.name: Polymers and Fibres
learn: Kevlar (aramid) in bulletproof jackets and helmets
Melamine as a thermosetting plastic; rayon as artificial silk; biodegradable PHBV
chapters.note: Kevlar was asked in consecutive papers.

chapters.name: Metals, Ores and Alloys
learn: Ores: bauxite, corundum, cryolite (aluminium), limonite (iron), cinnabar (mercury)
Alloys: brass = copper + zinc
Reactivity series and displacement; rusting adds weight; noble metals
Smelting; galvanised iron

chapters.name: Atomic Structure and Periodic Table
learn: Protons, neutrons, electrons; mass number = protons + neutrons; isotopes
Models and theories: J. J. Thomson's model, Dalton's atomic theory
Technetium, the first artificial element
Sigma and pi bonds in benzene

chapters.name: Motion, Force and Gravitation
learn: Newton's laws: inertia, F = ma, impulse; s = ½at²
Circular motion: centripetal force, centrifuge
Free fall: same acceleration for all masses; escape velocity; effect of the earth's rotation on weight
Friction: rolling versus sliding; viscosity; floating ice
chapters.note: Asked in almost every paper.

chapters.name: Light and Optics
learn: Mirrors: images by a concave mirror, focal length of a plane mirror
Lenses: convex lens as magnifier, partly covered lens, resolving power of a telescope
Refraction: speed and refractive index, frequency unchanged, twinkling of stars
Interference in soap films; shadows; mixing colours
chapters.note: Asked in almost every paper.

chapters.name: Electricity and Magnetism
learn: Ohm's law; resistors in parallel; power P = VI = I²R = V²/R
Fuse and short circuit
Dynamo versus transformer; capacitive reactance and frequency
Conducting liquids; energy eV gained by a charge; para- and ferromagnetic materials
chapters.note: Asked in almost every paper.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Waves and Modern Physics
learn: Electromagnetic waves: speed 3 × 10⁸ m/s; infrared for heat therapy; X-rays are not deflected by fields
Nuclear: fusion in the hydrogen bomb; alpha rays
Photoelectric cell; semiconductors (resistance falls on heating)
Solar constant
chapters.note: Infrared heat therapy was asked more than once.

chapters.name: Units, Instruments and Scientists
learn: Units: tesla (magnetic field), light-year (distance)
Scalars versus vectors
Instruments: galvanometer, odometer
Scientists: Einstein, Galileo

chapters.name: Heat and Thermodynamics
learn: Everyday heat: pressure cooker, refrigerator door, fan and evaporation, steam burns (latent heat)
Radiation needs no medium; conductors of heat

chapters.name: Sound
learn: Pitch depends on frequency; tension of a string
Speed of sound highest in solids; ultrasound in medicine

chapters.name: Work, Energy and Power
learn: Work = force × distance; conservation of energy for a falling body

chapters.name: Human Body Systems
learn: Digestion: HCl in the stomach, bile into the duodenum, carbohydrates to glucose
Endocrine: ductless glands, pituitary at the base of the brain, estrogen
Sense organs: five basic tastes including umami
Muscles work in pairs and only pull; cartilage

chapters.name: Plant Physiology
learn: Photosynthesis: chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light; dark reaction in the stroma
Water transport: osmosis in roots, transpiration pull, stomata and guard cells; xylem versus phloem
Nutrition: phosphorus for root growth; insectivorous plants in nitrogen-poor soil
Pollination; halophytes; respiration at night
chapters.note: Asked in most papers.

chapters.name: Plant Morphology and Useful Plants
learn: Which plant part we use: ginger and turmeric (rhizome, a stem), clove (flower bud), mango (mesocarp), apple (false fruit, thalamus), quinine (Cinchona bark)
Stems, buds and growth: apical meristems, trees versus shrubs
Natural fibres and sources: linen (flax), coir (coconut), mohair (Angora goat)
chapters.note: A BPSC favourite: "which part of the plant" repeats across papers.

chapters.name: Classification and Microorganisms
learn: Fungi lack chlorophyll; lichen is alga plus fungus; mycorrhiza
Decomposition by bacteria and other microorganisms; viruses as intracellular parasites
Gymnosperms (conifers); de Candolle and plant classification
Earthworm: haemoglobin dissolved in plasma

chapters.name: Blood and Immunity
learn: Blood groups: antigens on red cells; AB universal acceptor; ABO and Rh matching
Plasma as the fluid part of blood
Immunity: lymphocytes; antibodies made by B cells; IgM appears first
chapters.note: Asked in most papers.

chapters.name: Cell and Genetics
learn: Cell as the structural and functional unit of life; membranes of lipids and proteins
Chloroplasts have their own DNA
DNA double helix (Watson and Crick); mRNA; start codon AUG and stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA
Most enzymes are proteins

chapters.name: Vitamins and Nutrition
learn: Fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) versus water-soluble (B-complex, C) vitamins; liver storage
Vitamin K for blood clotting; milk is poor in vitamin C; legumes are rich in protein

chapters.name: Diseases and Their Causes
learn: Mosquito vectors: Anopheles (malaria) versus Culex, and how to tell them apart
Disease, organ and cause: pneumonia (lungs), anthrax, taeniasis (tapeworm), goitre (iodine), scurvy (vitamin C)
Treatment and tests: chloroquine for malaria, BCG for TB, Ishihara test for colour blindness
Medical terms: anorexia, insomnia, dyspnoea, anosmia

chapters.name: Vaccines and Medical Discoveries
learn: Edward Jenner and the smallpox vaccine (1796)
How vaccines work, including vector vaccines
Nobel-winning medical discoveries (dopamine and Parkinson's disease)

chapters.name: Space and Astronomy
learn: Missions and targets: Cassini (Saturn), Juno (Jupiter), VERITAS (Venus), Artemis (Moon); Apollo 11
Pulsars are rotating neutron stars; comets have elongated orbits

chapters.name: Emerging Technologies
learn: 5G: Internet of Things, edge computing, network slicing
Indian robots such as Manav

chapters.name: Computers and Artificial Intelligence
learn: Full forms: GPT - Generative Pre-trained Transformer
Names of programming languages (Python, Java)
chapters.note: Rare in BPSC.

chapters.name: Heritage, Culture and Environment in News
learn: UNESCO recognitions: Kozhikode, India's first City of Literature (2023)
Classical languages: Marathi, Bengali and others added in October 2024
Environment news: Blue Flag beaches, vulture conservation in Tamil Nadu, species releases in national parks
GI tags and food regulator decisions in news (Nihonshu application by Japan; FSSAI and Himalayan yak)
Monument conservation by ASI; commemorative coins
chapters.note: Kozhikode as City of Literature was asked in two consecutive papers.

chapters.name: Defence and Security
learn: Rafale: made by Dassault Aviation of France, inducted at Ambala Air Force Station
Indigenous systems: Rudram anti-radiation missile, Akashteer air defence control system, MBT Arjun, ATAGS
Joint exercises and their venues (JIMEX-24 with Japan at Yokosuka)
Defence events: DefExpo theme, Air Force Day venue; Galwan Valley clash (June 2020)

chapters.name: Reports, Indices and Surveys
learn: Who publishes which report: NITI Aayog (SDG India Index), MoSPI (Youth in India), World Bank (Human Capital Index, Ease of Doing Business), UNDP (Human Development Report)
India's latest rank or value and the top State or country (Kerala topped SDG India Index 2023-24; Singapore topped Human Capital Index 2020)
Swachh Survekshan top cities; Mother Tongue Survey of India (576 languages)
chapters.note: Learn publisher, India's rank and the topper for each index of the year.

chapters.name: Polity and Elections in News
learn: Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2019: passed 11 December 2019; covers persecuted minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan
Presidential election candidates (Yashwant Sinha, opposition candidate 2022)
Election Commission changes: postal ballot age for senior citizens raised to 85 (2024); Shompen tribe voting for the first time
Republic Day chief guest of the year; first State to implement a national policy (Uttarakhand and NEP)

chapters.name: Infrastructure and Projects
learn: Atal Tunnel at Rohtang: 9.02 km
New airports and their cities (Donyi Polo Airport, Itanagar)
Central Vista Project and the new Parliament building (built by Tata Projects)
Undersea cable projects such as Chennai-Andaman and Nicobar

chapters.name: Economy and Budget in News
learn: Union Budget of the year: stated priorities and headline schemes (nine priorities of 2024-25; oilseed self-reliance crops)
Corporate milestones (Reliance first Indian company to cross USD 200 billion market capitalisation)
Apps and products launched by banks (HDFC Bank e-Kisaan Dhan)

chapters.name: World Events and Politics
learn: US politics: Joe Biden as 46th President, attempt on Donald Trump at Butler, Pennsylvania (2024)
Assassinations and deaths: Shinzo Abe (2022), Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran (2024)
Places in news: Mauna Loa eruption, Sakteng Sanctuary in Bhutan, Yala Glacier of Nepal declared dead
Afghanistan withdrawal 2021; first Arab nuclear power plant (Barakah, UAE)
Odd one-off facts: Titan submersible implosion (2023), Collins word of the year, New Zealand's Plain Language Act
chapters.note: Mostly current affairs: follow the last 12 months, especially where an event took place.

chapters.name: Summits and Conferences
learn: G20 summits by number, year and host: 18th in New Delhi (2023), 19th in Rio de Janeiro (2024)
Climate COPs: COP27 (drought alliance by Spain and Senegal), COP28 in Dubai, COP29 in Baku (USD 300 billion a year by 2035)
WTO Ministerial Conference (13th in Abu Dhabi, 2024); World Economic Forum at Davos; AI Action Summit in Paris (2025)
ASEAN and BRICS meetings: host country and who represented India
UN Ocean Conference 2022 and its Lisbon Declaration
chapters.note: Asked in almost every recent paper: learn host city, number and year together.

chapters.name: International Organisations in News
learn: India at the UN Security Council: non-permanent term from 1 January 2021, presidency in August 2021
New members and chairs: Sweden as 32nd NATO member (2024), Russia chairing BRICS (2024), India chairing the ILO Governing Body (2020-21)
UN General Assembly in news: emergency session on Ukraine, multilingualism resolution mentioning Hindi (2022), vetoes in the Security Council
Members of groupings such as the Quad (India, Japan, Australia, USA)

chapters.name: India's Agreements and Foreign Relations
learn: India's trade pacts: ECTA with Australia (2022)
